title: The Gunpowder Plot, 1605 — 36 barrels, one letter, and a man called John Johnson
sources: Wikipedia: Gunpowder Plot — Robert Catesby proposed to kill the king and his government by blowing up 'the Parliament House with gunpowder'; Fawkes, using the pseudonym 'John Johnson', took charge of the building posing as Thomas Percy's servant; according to Fawkes, 20 barrels of gunpowder were brought in at first, then 16 more; on 26 October 1605 an anonymous letter was delivered to Lord Monteagle, a Catholic peer, warning: 'they shall receive a terrible blow this Parliament; and yet they shall not see who hurts them'; Monteagle showed it to the authorities; the conspirators thought it a hoax and carried on; in a search on the night of 4–5 November Fawkes was found guarding 36 barrels of gunpowder, enough to reduce the House of Lords to rubble; he gave his name as John Johnson; the king decided he would be tortured; people lit bonfires around London to celebrate the king's survival

Wikipedia: Guy Fawkes — he carried a lantern now in the Ashmolean Museum, Oxford, and a search revealed a pocket watch, slow matches and touchwood; his scrawled signature suggests what he suffered; weakened by torture, he jumped from the gallows and broke his neck
Wikipedia: Guy Fawkes Night — 5 November is commemorated in Britain with bonfires and fireworks
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1854 the Battle of Inkerman; 2013 India launches its Mars Orbiter Mission

Pictures (public domain): the conspirators, engraving by Crispijn van de Passe; the Monteagle letter; Fawkes's lantern; the undercroft beneath the House of Lords; Capon's plan of the old Palace of Westminster; Fawkes's signatures before and after torture; the execution of the plotters; a Guy Fawkes Night bonfire at Windsor; Punch, 1850
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): wooden barrels, an oil lantern, a bonfire, fireworks

post.facebook:
On this day in 1605, the Gunpowder Plot was foiled.

A group of Catholic conspirators led by Robert Catesby planned to blow up King James and his government. They rented a cellar beneath the House of Lords and filled it with gunpowder, guarded by a soldier named Guy Fawkes, posing as a servant called John Johnson.

Ten days earlier, Lord Monteagle, a Catholic peer, had received an anonymous letter: "They shall receive a terrible blow this Parliament; and yet they shall not see who hurts them." He took it to the authorities. The plotters heard about it — and decided it was a hoax.

Late on the night of 4–5 November the cellar was searched. There was Fawkes, with a lantern, slow matches and 36 barrels of gunpowder — enough to reduce the House of Lords to rubble. He gave his name as John Johnson. The king ordered him tortured; his shaking signature shows what it did to him.

That night, Londoners lit bonfires to celebrate the king's survival. Britain still does, every 5th of November.

Also on 5 November: the Battle of Inkerman (1854), and India's Mars Orbiter Mission (2013).

youtube.description:
5 November 1605: the Gunpowder Plot was foiled. Robert Catesby's conspirators had packed 36 barrels of gunpowder into a cellar under the House of Lords, guarded by Guy Fawkes posing as "John Johnson". An anonymous letter warned Lord Monteagle of "a terrible blow this Parliament" — the plotters thought it was a hoax. Late that night the cellar was searched and Fawkes was caught with a lantern and slow matches. The king ordered him tortured, and London lit bonfires — the start of Bonfire Night.

Also on 5 November: the Battle of Inkerman (1854) and India's Mars Orbiter Mission (2013).
